chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Writing "Moon Ray" with Artie Shaw at the Brickwood
summary: McRae recalls Shaw hanging out in Harlem and the bass part he gave him for a theme; he praises Shaw as arranger and clarinetist.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How about "Moon Ray"? What role did you have in composing that song?

Well, we were sitting down in Brickwood, like I told you before. We were sitting down in Brickwood Cafe, right across the street from Broadway. Artie Shaw used to come uptown all the time. At that time, you know, a lot of musicians
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

came uptown to hear, you know, to listen to the jazz musicians. Because you remember, those days that was really the cream of the crop of American jazz. Like when Fletcher Henderson and, you know, Small's Paradise -- MR. WELBURN: Duke? You know, Charlie Johnson -- all those bands were around, you know. Don Redman, you know. "chart of (Unintelligible) the Weed man. You know, those are heavy duty stuff, you know. And all of the band leaders come uptown to Harlem. That's when Harlem was the glorious showcase of the world. People came from all over Europe to come to Harlem. And Artie Shaw used to come up and hang out with us, you know. One day we was down in the basement over there -- the little club, the Brickwood -- and Artie -- Chick had Artie and Artie and I were sitting there talking.

He say, "You know, we're going to open up in Boston the same time." (Inaudible) this going to be my theme song."
He says, "You play this part and I'll play the clarinet part."
So I played the bass part (Inaudible). He say, "You're writing it, this going to be my theme song. Go on, put your name on it." I say, "Nah, nah," (inaudible)."
And he (inaudible) up. Artie Shaw is a very good writer and a good arranger. He was a very good arranger. Concert (Inaudible) musician. Concert (Inaudible) clarinet.
And a number of recordings with strings?
